identity.title: Monthly EHS Self-Check
agencies: U.S. Department of Labor - Occupational Safety and Health Administration

scan.summary: This is a monthly self-inspection checklist designed to track compliance with workplace safety, air quality, fire safety, and chemical handling standards. The company completes this form to verify that key controls are in place each month — air permit posted and valid, scrubber pressure-drop readings logged within operating ranges, detector-tube checks performed, equipment inspections done, fire extinguishers current, exits clear, eyewash and safety showers functional, and safety data sheets available. Any item marked 'N' must be reported to the Plant Manager by the 5th of the following month.
scan.freshness_note: The document is a blank template with no completion date, month, signatures, or data filled in. It cannot be assessed for timeliness or adherence to any deadline without a completed instance showing which month was reviewed and what the results were.

gaps.title: No document date or completion record visible
gaps.description: The template shows blanks for Month, Completed by, and Supervisor with no dates or initials filled in. Without a completed instance of this form, it is not possible to verify whether the company is performing these checks or how recent the most recent check was.
gaps.fix: Obtain a completed monthly self-check form showing the month reviewed, the date of supervisor review, the employee who completed it, and the results (Y/N and initials) for each line item. Confirm the company fills this out every month.
gaps.citation: OSHA General Duty Clause (OSH Act Section 5(a)(1)); OAR 340-216-8010 et seq. (Oregon air permit posting and availability requirements)
gaps.locator: entire document — no dates filled in

gaps.title: No procedure for tracking or escalating failures
gaps.description: The form states 'Items marked N are reported to the Plant Manager by the 5th of the following month' but does not specify what happens next — no procedure for investigation, root cause, corrective action, documentation, or verification that issues are fixed before the next month.
gaps.fix: Establish a written procedure defining: (1) what constitutes an 'N' result, (2) who investigates, (3) required corrective actions by category, (4) documentation requirements, (5) verification that fixes are in place before the next check, (6) escalation criteria for repeated failures or safety risks.
gaps.citation: OSHA General Duty Clause; 29 CFR 1910.22 (general safety requirements); Oregon DEQ permit conditions typically require prompt correction of deficiencies
gaps.quote: Items marked N are reported to the Plant Manager by the 5th of the following month.

gaps.title: Missing scope for Line 3 — C-1 detector-tube check frequency and method
gaps.description: Line 3 calls for 'Weekly C-1 detector-tube checks done and recorded every week this month' but the checklist does not specify what constitutes a valid check (e.g., testing method, recording format, pass/fail criteria, action if outlet exceeds threshold).
gaps.fix: Add to the procedure or attach a reference document: the standard or protocol for C-1 outlet detector-tube testing, the acceptable range or pass criterion, the required log format, and what corrective action is required if the check shows a failure.
gaps.citation: Oregon air permit conditions for scrubber outlet monitoring (likely specified in Permit 26-2841-ST-01 or its attachments); ANSI/ASABE standard or equivalent
gaps.quote: Weekly C-1 detector-tube checks done and recorded every week this month

gaps.title: Missing acceptance range for Line 2 — scrubber pressure-drop readings
gaps.description: Line 2 specifies 'readings between 2.0 and 6.0' but does not clarify the units (inches water column, bar, kPa, etc.) or reference the source permit condition that sets this range.
gaps.fix: Amend Line 2 to state the units of measurement (e.g., 'readings between 2.0 and 6.0 inches of water column') and add a reference to the permit condition or design document that establishes this range.
gaps.citation: Oregon air permit conditions for scrubber operations; company's own Scrubber Pressure-Drop Log document already exists

gaps.title: No definition of defect follow-up documentation for Line 4
gaps.description: Line 4 requires 'any defect followed up' but does not specify what follow-up means — repair timelines, work orders, log entries, supervisor approval, or sign-off required.
gaps.fix: Add to the procedure or manual: define 'follow-up' to include (1) creation of work order or incident report, (2) severity/urgency category, (3) repair deadline (e.g., before next use, within 24 hours, within one week), (4) required documentation (photos, maintenance log entry, mechanic's sign-off), and (5) verification that defect was corrected before the truck next runs.
gaps.citation: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178 (powered industrial truck operation and maintenance); company's own PIT Pre-Shift Inspection Log already documents daily checks

gaps.title: Fire extinguisher tag protocol not specified
gaps.description: Line 5 states fire extinguishers must be 'tagged within the last 12 months; monthly visual check initialled on each tag' but does not specify who performs the monthly check (technician or any employee), where initials go, or what visual checks constitute pass/fail.
gaps.fix: Add procedures for fire extinguisher maintenance: (1) annual professional inspection/recharge must be performed by a certified service company; (2) monthly visual walk-through: check for damage, blockage, pressure gauge in green zone; (3) log and initial a tag on the extinguisher or maintain a separate log; (4) any defect triggers immediate service or replacement. Reference NFPA 10 or equivalent.
gaps.citation: NFPA 10 (Standard for Portable Fire Extinguishers); OSHA 29 CFR 1910.157 (general requirements for all portable fire extinguishers)
gaps.quote: tagged within the last 12 months; monthly visual check initialled on each tag

gaps.title: Eyewash and safety shower flush protocol incomplete
gaps.description: Line 7 calls for 'Eyewash stations and safety showers flushed this week and logged' but does not specify duration of flush, acceptance criteria, or where logs are kept.
gaps.fix: Add to the procedure: (1) flushing frequency (at minimum weekly; some standards require daily or when in use); (2) flush duration (typically 1–3 minutes to clear lines); (3) visual inspection for water flow, clarity, and nozzle function; (4) log entry must include date, time, location, flush duration, any defects noted, and initials; (5) any malfunction must trigger repair/replacement before next work day.
gaps.citation: ANSI Z535.4 (labeling and marking of hazardous substances); OSHA 29 CFR 1910.151 (eye and face protection); many states and facilities follow ANSI Z535.1 or local code for emergency equipment inspection
gaps.quote: Eyewash stations and safety showers flushed this week and logged

gaps.title: SDS binder update protocol undefined
gaps.description: Line 8 requires 'Safety data sheets on hand for every chemical received this month; binder index updated' but does not define who updates the index, how indexing is organized, or how obsolete SDSs are removed.
gaps.fix: Add to the SDS management procedure: (1) designate responsible person(s); (2) require SDS to be obtained and added to binder within X days of receipt (commonly within 5–10 days); (3) organize by product name, CAS number, or hazard category with consistent labeling; (4) maintain an index or log with product name, receipt date, SDS version date, and location in binder; (5) remove and archive obsolete SDSs (keep for X years per record retention policy); (6) verify accessibility during inspections; (7) train all employees on binder location and use.
gaps.citation: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(g) (Hazard Communication Standard, SDS requirements)
gaps.quote: Safety data sheets on hand for every chemical received this month; binder index updated

facts.value: 8 line items covering air permit, scrubber monitoring, detector-tube checks, forklift inspections, fire extinguisher maintenance, exit routes, eyewash/safety showers, and safety data sheets
facts.affects: The breadth of the monthly check spans air quality, fire protection, chemical safety, and mechanical equipment maintenance, indicating the facility operates under multiple regulatory regimes (OSHA, DEQ air permit, NFPA fire codes).

expected_missing.title: Completed monthly forms for prior months
expected_missing.why: To verify the company is actually conducting these checks monthly and responding to failures, a history of completed forms is essential. Without them, the template is a procedure document only, not evidence of compliance.
expected_missing.basis: industry best practice; OSHA expects employers to maintain records of inspections and corrective actions.

expected_missing.title: Escalation or investigation log for 'N' results
expected_missing.why: The checklist states failures go to the Plant Manager by the 5th of the following month, but no log of those reports, investigations, or remediation actions was provided. This is critical evidence that problems are addressed.
expected_missing.basis: OSHA General Duty Clause and permit conditions typically require documentation of corrective action.

expected_missing.title: Scrubber maintenance and testing SOP
expected_missing.why: Line 2 and 3 reference specific monitoring ranges and detector-tube checks, but the actual procedure, acceptance criteria, and corrective-action thresholds are not attached or incorporated.
expected_missing.basis: Air permit conditions and company's own Scrubber Pressure-Drop Log document suggest these details exist elsewhere.

expected_missing.title: Fire extinguisher maintenance contract or service record
expected_missing.why: Line 5 requires annual professional tagging and monthly checks. The company should hold a service contract and annual maintenance records, which are missing from the submission.
expected_missing.basis: NFPA 10 and OSHA 1910.157 require documentation of professional inspections.

expected_missing.title: SDS master list or binder with current index
expected_missing.why: Line 8 requires an updated SDS binder and index. The template does not show how many chemicals are in inventory or what the current index looks like.
expected_missing.basis: OSHA 1910.1200(g) requires ready access to SDSs for all hazardous chemicals in use.

expected_missing.title: Exit route and emergency egress audit or floor plan
expected_missing.why: Line 6 checks that exits and aisles are clear and signs are lit, but no floor plan, exit signage documentation, or periodic egress audit procedure is provided.
expected_missing.basis: OSHA 1910.35 requires workplace emergency action plans and exit route maintenance.

expected_missing.title: Powered Industrial Truck operator training and evaluation records
expected_missing.why: The company has a 'Powered Industrial Truck Operator Training and Evaluation Record' in its document list, but how that links to the pre-shift inspection protocol on Line 4 is not shown.
expected_missing.basis: OSHA 1910.178 requires operators to be trained and evaluated, and daily pre-shift checks to be documented.

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence that this is a template self-inspection checklist. The form itself is well-structured and addresses key regulatory areas. However, because no completed instance is provided, it is not possible to assess whether the company is using this form, how frequently, or whether they are responding to deficiencies. The gaps listed are process and definition gaps — the template uses terminology like 'readings between 2.0 and 6.0,' 'weekly checks,' and 'followed up,' but does not specify units, methods, timelines, or documentation standards. This is typical of a form that is used in conjunction with other SOPs or manuals not provided here. Medium-to-low confidence in whether the company's actual monitoring and response practices meet regulatory requirements without seeing those SOPs, completed forms, and failure-response logs.

CASCADE SPECIALTY CHEMICALS, LLC — PORTLAND FACILITY

MONTHLY EHS SELF-CHECK

Month: __________ Completed by: ____________________ Supervisor: ____________________

Line

Check

Done (Y/N)

Initials

Notes

1

Air permit posted in the front office and not expired

2

Scrubber pressure-drop log complete for the month, every operating day, readings between 2.0 and 6.0

3

Weekly C-1 detector-tube checks done and recorded every week this month

4

Forklift pre-shift inspection log complete for every day the truck ran; any defect followed up

5

Fire extinguishers tagged within the last 12 months; monthly visual check initialled on each tag

6

Exits, exit routes and aisles clear; exit signs lit

7

Eyewash stations and safety showers flushed this week and logged

8

Safety data sheets on hand for every chemical received this month; binder index updated

Supervisor review: ____________________ Date: __________ · Items marked N are reported to the Plant Manager by the 5th of the following month.
